pr_title: Feature(bubble-memo): run the memo reviewer only on request
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 7 of 7 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: The driver tests are behavioral: they run bubble_memo.main in-process against throwaway git projects and read real stdout/stderr, and nothing is stubbed.

The new flag is covered on all three paths: off by default on a clean check (no row), on request on a clean check (row printed), and on request on a failing check (no row). This matches the cmd_check gate at bubble_memo.py:509-512.
The existing model-selection tests (sonnet/opus flagging) were updated to pass --reviewer-row, so the per-entry flag still has coverage after the default changed.

The skill contract tests split SKILL.md into Steps and On request and check each one: the default flow names no reviewer, --reviewer-row or findings, and the reviewer dispatch lives only under On request. That pins the change in section placement rather than relying on whole-body substrings.
The module docstring, usage block and argparse help for `check --pr N [--reviewer-row]` all match cmd_check, which prints the row only under the flag (bubble_memo.py:25-27, 37, 511-512, 525-527).
The flag is registered only on the check subparser, so scaffold and the other commands cannot receive it by accident; the default keeps `check [ok]` output and exit codes unchanged.

The new `--reviewer-row` flag in SKILL.md:130 matches the driver exactly: argparse at bubble_memo.py:526-527, it prints only after a clean check (bubble_memo.py:511-512), and the module docstring (bubble_memo.py:25-27,37) documents it.
The default flow drops the reviewer entirely. The steps renumber cleanly (5 then 6) with no dangling 'step 7' references, and the contract test pins that Steps never names the reviewer.

The agent description now says outright that the skill never dispatches it by default, and its first example uses the request phrasing ('review the bubble memo') and the flagged command. The trigger matches the skill.

The second-round rule moves from an implicit trigger ('only when the first returned an accuracy finding') to the developer's explicit request. That removes a judgment call the session used to make on its own.
The driver change is small: `--reviewer-row` only gates the print, after the clean-check raise path, so a failing check can never leak a dispatch row (bubble_memo.py:507-512).
All three new driver tests are behavioral and run the real `main` against throwaway projects: no row by default, a row on request, and no row from a failing check even with the flag.
The skill contract tests split the Steps section from the On request section, so the default flow is checked to never mention the reviewer, the flag or findings.

The module docstring, usage block, argparse help, agent description example and SKILL.md were all updated in the same commit for the new flag, and the two flag-dependent model-selection tests now pass `--reviewer-row` explicitly instead of losing their coverage.

important.name: Snapshot rule says a decision stamp is the only change after hand-off; On request edits the memo after hand-off
important.summary:
SKILL.md:29-30 now says 'The one change after hand-off is a decision stamp'. The new 'On request' section (lines 124-140) tells the session to open each reviewer finding's location in the memo and correct it, and the reviewer agent's second example ('review the memo again', bubble-memo-reviewer.md:19-22) shows that review arriving after an earlier hand-off. A session that follows the snapshot rule as written must either refuse to apply the reviewer's corrections or break the rule. The PR added both texts, so the skill now contradicts itself on the exact flow it introduces.

Also (roast): SKILL.md:29-30 now says the one change to the memo after hand-off is a decision stamp. The default flow ends at step 6 (Hand off, SKILL.md:120-122), so a review the developer asks for afterwards runs after hand-off, and SKILL.md:137-138 tells the session to open each finding's location and correct the memo. Whenever the review is asked for after the hand-off, the skill breaks its own rule. The section also never says when it runs relative to step 6: it ends with 'Report the findings left unapplied ... in the hand-off' (SKILL.md:139-140), which assumes it runs before the hand-off, but step 5 has already declared 'the work is done' (SKILL.md:118) and step 6 has no hook for it. A request that arrives as invocation guidance ('-- and review it') therefore has no defined place in the flow. Two rules, one memo, and the agent gets to pick which one to break.

Also (docs): SKILL.md:29 says the decision stamp is the 'next rule'. This PR inserts the new 'One pass, no review cycle' rule at line 31, right after it. The decision-stamping rule is now three bullets down, at line 38, after the References and prose rules. The cross-reference sends the reader to the rule about review cycles.

Also (roast): SKILL.md:29 calls the decision stamp 'the next rule', but the bullet right after it is the new 'One pass, no review cycle' (SKILL.md:31-32). The decision-stamp rule is three bullets further down, at SKILL.md:38-40. Inserting the new bullet in between turned a correct cross-reference into a wrong one.
fix: Rewrite SKILL.md:29-30 to: 'The only changes after hand-off are a decision stamp (the decision-stamping rule below) and the corrections from a review the developer asks for (section "On request").'
Alternatively, scope the On request section to before hand-off and say a review after hand-off is a fresh memo edit the developer authorizes, then make the snapshot rule name that exception.

Reword SKILL.md:29-30 to allow both changes, e.g. 'After hand-off the memo changes only by a decision stamp (rule "Decision stamping is not this skill's job") or by corrections from a review the developer asked for (section "On request").' Then state the timing in the On request section: when the invocation's guidance asks for a review, run it between steps 5 and 6 and fold the unapplied findings into the step 6 hand-off; when the developer asks after hand-off, run it then and report the unapplied findings in a short follow-up.

Alternatively, make the review a pre-hand-off step only: add to step 5 'when the developer asked for a review, run section "On request" before step 6', and say in On request that a review requested after hand-off counts as a new run that starts from step 5.
Replace '(next rule)' with '(rule "Decision stamping is not this skill's job")', or with 'the decision-stamping rule below'.
Or move the 'Decision stamping is not this skill's job' bullet up so it directly follows the snapshot rule.
Replace '(next rule)' with '(rule "Decision stamping is not this skill's job" below)'.
Or move the 'One pass, no review cycle' bullet below the decision-stamping bullet (SKILL.md:38-40), so the decision-stamping rule follows the snapshot rule again.

important.name: New snapshot/decision-stamp contract test passes on the pre-PR skill
important.summary:
test_the_memo_stays_a_snapshot_apart_from_decision_stamps (tests/skills/test_bubble_memo_skill_contract.py:91-94) checks only that 'snapshot', 'bubble-stamp' and 'Hand off' appear somewhere in the body. All three were already in SKILL.md at the merge base (the snapshot rule, the decision-stamping rule, step 8 'Hand off'). So the test passes with or without the clause this PR added at SKILL.md:29-30, and deleting that clause would leave it green. Its name promises a guard on the decision-stamp exception that it does not provide.

Also (tests): test_the_memo_stays_a_snapshot_apart_from_decision_stamps asserts only that 'snapshot', 'bubble-stamp' and 'Hand off' appear anywhere in the body. All three strings are present in the merge-base SKILL.md (lines 27, 35, 128), and 'snapshot' is also covered by test_the_skill_keeps_prose_and_the_snapshot_rule, so the new test does not guard the rule the PR introduced: the Rules bullet 'One pass, no review cycle' (SKILL.md:31-32) that says no reviewer runs unless the developer asks. Its name promises a separation (the memo stays a snapshot apart from decision stamps) that whole-body substring checks cannot detect.
fix: Pin the new clause: take the snapshot-rule bullet (the text from '**The memo is a point-in-time snapshot**' to the next '\n- **') and assert that 'decision stamp' and 'after hand-off' are in it, in place of the three body-wide substring checks.
Alternatively, assert the exact sentence: assert "The one change after hand-off is a decision stamp" in body.

Scope the assertions to the Rules section (split on '\n## Rules' and '\n## Steps') and assert the new 'One pass, no review cycle' rule and its 'unless the developer asks' clause there, alongside 'bubble-stamp' and 'snapshot'.
Fold the 'bubble-stamp' and 'Hand off' checks into test_the_skill_keeps_prose_and_the_snapshot_rule and drop the duplicate test.

minor.name: Step 5 ends the work even when the invocation itself asked for a review
minor.summary:
Step 5 (SKILL.md:118) ends with 'the work is done', and step 6 hands off. If the developer asks for a review in the same invocation (for example in the guidance after `--`), the On request section applies, but no step points to it. On request (line 140) then says to report unapplied findings 'in the hand-off', which step 6 has already delivered. A session that follows the steps in order may hand off and never run the requested review, or hand off twice.

Also (docs): On request (SKILL.md:138) says 'Run `check` again until it is clean' right after the session ran `check --pr <N> --reviewer-row`. The command is not spelled out. If the session reruns the last command with the flag, every clean check prints a fresh reviewer row, and the step 2 dispatch pattern invites a second dispatch. That conflicts with 'One round is the whole review' on the next line.
fix: In step 5, after 'check [ok]', add: 'When the invocation asked for a review, run section "On request" before the hand-off.' Avoid the words that test_the_default_flow_has_no_review_cycle bans from Steps ('reviewer row', 'findings', '--reviewer-row', 'bubble-memo-reviewer', 'review round').
Or reword On request line 139-140 to 'Report the findings left unapplied, with the reason, to the developer (in the hand-off when the review ran in the same invocation).'
Change it to 'Run `check` again without `--reviewer-row` (the step 5 command) until it is clean.'

minor.name: Failing-check test checks only 'agent=', not the Memo line
minor.summary: test_a_failing_check_prints_no_reviewer_row_even_on_request asserts `"agent=" not in out`. The default-path test (line 161) also asserts `"Memo:" not in out`. A regression that printed the Memo path but not the agent line on a failing check would slip past it.
fix: Extend line 176 with `and "Memo:" not in out`, matching the assertion at line 161.

minor.name: Stray whitespace removal around '=' in an unrelated line
minor.summary: The diff changes `chain = "- **Chain:** ...` to `chain ="- **Chain:** ...` at line 275. Nothing else in the hunk needs it; it breaks PEP 8 spacing (pycodestyle E225) and adds noise to the diff.
fix:
Restore the space: `chain = "- **Chain:** step one
  ```
  a -> b
  ```
"`.

minor.name: _split_steps fails with a bare unpack error when a heading is missing
minor.summary: If SKILL.md loses or renames '## On request', `steps, rest = steps.split(...)` raises 'ValueError: not enough values to unpack'. If '## Steps' goes missing, `[1]` raises IndexError. Both tests built on the helper then error out instead of failing with a message that names the missing section, so the cause is hard to see from CI output.
fix: Assert that each heading is present before splitting, e.g. `assert "\n## Steps" in body, "Steps section missing"` and `assert "\n## On request" in steps, "On request section missing"`.
